'''Wang Yening''' ({{zh|s=王业宁}}; 14 October 1926 – 22 February 2019), also known as '''Ye-Ning (Y. N.) Wang''', was a Chinese physicist. She was an educator with a specialization in [[condensed matter physics]]. She spent her entire career at [[Nanjing University]] and was elected an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1991. She was a recipient of the [[State Natural Science Award]] (Second Class) and the [[Ho Leung Ho Lee Prize]] in Physics.

== Biography ==
Wang was born on 14 October 1926 in [[Anqing]], [[Anhui]], [[Republic of China (1912–1949)|Republic of China]]. She studied at the Department of Physics of [[National Central University]] (NCU) in [[Nanjing]] from 1945 to 1949, and became an assistant professor of [[Nanjing University]] (reorganized from the former NCU) in 1950. She spent her entire career at Nanjing University, and was later promoted to lecturer, associate professor, and eventually professor.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_3041588|language=zh-hans|script-title=zh:中科院院士王业宁逝世，南京城一日内痛失两位重量级女院士|last=Yue|first=Huairang|date=26 February 2019|website=The Paper|access-date=27 February 2019}}</ref>

In 1953, Wang studied metal physics and [[internal friction]] under [[Ke T'ing-sui]] (Ge Tingsui) at the Institute of Metal Research of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. She returned to Nanjing University a year later and helped [[Cheng Kaijia]] and Shi Shiyuan establish China's first X-ray metal physics program.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.hlhl.org.cn/english/showsub.asp?id=330|title=Wang Yening|website=Ho Leung Ho Lee Foundation|access-date=27 February 2019}}</ref>

Wang's research focuses included general [[phase transition]]s, behaviours of [[Crystallographic defect|crystallographic surface defects]], [[superconductors]], and other areas of [[condensed matter physics]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> She published more than 200 scientific papers and was one of the world's top 150 authors in [[high-temperature superconductivity]] in the 1990s.<ref name=":1" /> She pioneered "Wang's theory" for her [[Coupling (physics)|coupling]] [[Relaxation (physics)|relaxation]] theory pertaining to the collective relaxation process of defects in [[alloy]]s.<ref name=":1" />

For her achievements, Wang was conferred the National Science and Technology Conference Award (1978), the [[State Natural Science Award]] (Second Class) in 1982, the Golden Ox Award (1994), and the [[Ho Leung Ho Lee Prize]] in Physics (2000).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> She was elected an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1991.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sohu.com/a/297763206_161795|language=zh-hans|script-title=zh:中科院院士、物理学家王业宁病逝！培养近百位硕士、博士及博士后|date=26 February 2019|website=Sohu|access-date=27 February 2019}}</ref>

In a career spanning more than half a century, she educated nearly 100 graduate students who earned master's or Ph.D. degrees as well as postdoctoral researchers. In 1993, she was named one of the "top ten women science and technology educators" by the [[Jiangsu]] Provincial Government.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
Wang was married to Lin Xingshan ({{lang|zh|林醒山}}; 1925–2016), who was a professor and Chair of the [[Civil Engineering]] Department of [[Southeast University]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mmcs.org.cn/gz/1224/2983/2016-06/139894.shtml|language=zh-hans|script-title=zh:王业宁院士—南京大学|date=30 June 2016|website=National Museum for Modern Chinese Scientists|access-date=27 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://civil.seu.edu.cn/2016/1204/c1251a177574/page.htm|language=zh-hans|script-title=zh:沉痛悼念我们尊敬的老土木系主任林醒山教授|date=22 December 2016|website=Southeast University|access-date=27 February 2019}}</ref> During the [[Cultural Revolution]] (1966–1976), Lin was denounced as a [[capitalist roader]] and imprisoned. Wang was forced to perform hard labour on a farm and on construction sites in Nanjing, while also raising their children on her own.<ref name=":3" />

Wang died on 22 February 2019 in Nanjing, at the age of 92.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />
